### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4ce310b88e902c3844f0a709ceb2e277939dc31` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `849edeb0bc3a2ccfecb46bde6b507287e53b9c91` — the merge of head `6e8e34751d43a724f0f529a225e69954cad46f5a` into base `b4ce310b88e902c3844f0a709ceb2e277939dc31`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 849edeb0bc3a2ccfecb46bde6b507287e53b9c91 && git checkout 849edeb0bc3a2ccfecb46bde6b507287e53b9c91
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b4ce310b88e902c3844f0a709ceb2e277939dc31 6e8e34751d43a724f0f529a225e69954cad46f5a && git checkout -B drift-repro b4ce310b88e902c3844f0a709ceb2e277939dc31 && git merge --no-ff 6e8e34751d43a724f0f529a225e69954cad46f5a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b4ce310b88e902c3844f0a709ceb2e277939dc31
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6e8e34751d43a724f0f529a225e69954cad46f5a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/direct-share-grant-is-manual.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/vitest.config.ts, .changeset/direct-share-grant-is-manual.md, content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx + packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-record-share.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, docs/adr/0111-record-share-management-authority-and-verb-boundary.md (cited code outside the diff: read, not reviewed)

Read at 2026-11-15T17:36Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6897925330; lane request 6897918264 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented and dispatched by security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla. CI re-read by the seat after the last run completed: 67 runs, 41 success, 25 skipped, 1 cancelled (a superseded `Check Changeset` run; its other runs are green), none failed, none running.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule under review: a share of any kind other than manual exists only because a platform path running under a system context wrote it; a share a non-system caller grants is a manual share. Read against the tree at this head, door by door.

- **Service method.** `SharingService.grant` applies the rule on its non-system branch, and the branch is chosen by `context.isSystem` alone, so a caller with no context, an owner, a holder of Modify All and a platform administrator all take it. The tree REFUSES (`VALIDATION_FAILED`); it does not coerce. The PR body, the changeset and the docs sentence all say refuse, and all three agree with the code.
- **REST route.** `POST /data/:object/:id/shares` (`packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts`, plain and environment-scoped registration, one handler) is the only non-system caller of `grant` in the tree. It forwards both spellings of the second field, and the service judges what it forwards. The route file's own note that an inbound HTTP context never carries the system flag holds in the code read.
- **Update of an existing share.** There is no separate update door: a repeated grant is the same method and passes the same check before the upsert is reached, so the update half is covered by the same refusal.
- **Generic data doors on the share object (create, update, delete, bulk, import).** `sys_record_share` declares `enable.apiMethods` get and list only and `managedBy: 'engine-owned'`; neither is touched by this diff. The dogfood file pins the REST create at 405. Update, delete and the non-REST generic doors rest on those two pre-existing declarations and were read, not reviewed.
- **Actions, bulk or batch grant, seeds.** A grep of the head for callers of `grant` and for writers of the share table finds none outside the REST route and the rule evaluator. Nothing in `ui/`, `examples/` or `apps/` sends either field on the grant door, so AGENTS.md Post-Task step 4 is not engaged.
- **System callers keep their kinds.** The only system caller of `grant` is the rule evaluator (`sharing-rule-service.ts`), whose context is built from the service's system context; its branch is unchanged, and the control tests pin a system-written rule share with its source id, at the service and on the booted stack.
- **Readers of the kind.** Revocation, the rule reconcile and sweep, the explain engine and the list views of the share object are not in the diff and read the stored kind exactly as before. No reader changes its answer because of this head. The one moved reading is already inside the declared FROM/TO: a non-system re-grant that named a non-manual kind is refused like a first grant.
- **Rows stored before this head.** Left exactly as stored. The changeset says no stored row changes, which is true; see S1 for what it does not say.

Declaration, per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: both line-initial declarations are in the PR body and the changeset and agree (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`); the title carries the bang; the changeset carries the BREAKING banner, who moves, FROM 201 TO 400, the one-line remedy, a Not-moved paragraph, and exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, whose reasoning matches the diff (no schema key, export or stored shape moves). Complete for the narrowing itself.

Tests: the service suite pins eight refused shapes for an authorised caller and one for an unauthorised caller, each with no row and no read, plus five controls (absent, null, explicit manual with its revoke, system rule share, non-system revoke of that share). The dogfood file pins six refused shapes through the real route, three controls and the generic create door. The two removed tests pinned the accepting branch the rule removes; the manual upsert (one row on a repeated grant) stays pinned by the earlier "upserts on second call" test and the coexistence test.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — The disposition of shares stored before this head is declared only by implication. A row of a non-manual kind that a non-system caller wrote before the fix stays stored and stays in force, and the changeset's "no stored row changes" does not tell an operator that such rows may exist or what to do about them. Whether that sentence belongs in the public changeset or in the lane's own advisory is the security lane's call; it should exist in one of them before this lands. Detail is in the seat's private notes, not here.
- S2 (should-fix) — The published contract and the SDK still state less than the tree does. `ISharingService.grant`'s jsdoc in `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts` enumerates the non-system refusals and does not carry this one, and `shares.grant` in `packages/client/src/index.ts` still types both fields as free strings. The PR body names the client half as a separate change and files no issue for it; the spec half is not named at all. File the follow-up (one issue covering both) so the typed surface does not go on offering a call the service always refuses.
- N1 (nit) — The docs sentence, the changeset and the new jsdoc name "sharing-rule, team and system paths" as writers of non-manual shares. In this tree the rule evaluator is the only such writer; no team or inherited path writes a share. "The platform's own paths under a system context" says what is true without naming writers that do not exist.
- N2 (nit) — The refusal judges `input.source` and `input.sourceId` in a helper, while the write uses values read from the input at other points. Passing the helper the values that are written would bind the check to the write by construction.
- N3 (nit) — No test names a non-system caller that holds the widest non-system authority (Modify All, platform administrator). The check precedes authorization, so the answer is the same by construction; a named control would keep it so.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch` is the level AGENTS.md prescribes: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes patch, and a non-protocol breaking change ships patch and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition, both present. No other package is moved by the diff (`packages/rest`, `packages/spec` and `packages/client` are not edited), so no other changeset is owed.

CI at this head, first read by the reviewer at 2026-11-15T16:56Z: 65 check-runs; 30 success, 25 skipped, 9 IN PROGRESS (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace), 0 failed, 1 cancelled (a superseded Check Changeset run; three later runs of it are green). Green so far includes Check Changeset, Lint and Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Build Core, Type Check source and consumer gates, Spec property liveness, the queue guard. The Dogfood Regression Gate job is green but its three shards are SKIPPED on this head, so the new dogfood file has no CI run here; its evidence is the implementer's local battery reported in the PR body, which this review did not re-run.

This PASS is rendered while checks are still running. The seat must wait for Test Core and Type Check · workspace to finish green before acting on it; a red there voids nothing in this record but blocks the landing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No governed path and no published schema in the diff; the face is the declared narrowing alone.
- `packages/rest` is covered by the service rule and not edited; its behaviour change (400 on the grant route) is declared in the changeset under the plugin's name.
- Security discipline: this record stays at the rule layer. Nothing here describes a mechanism; the notes that do are private to the seat.
- The generic-door closure for the share object rests on declarations outside this diff (ADR-0103); this review read them and did not review them.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: it makes the spec's own statement real rather than taking a declared capability away. The contract already describes `grant` as "Create or upsert a manual share row" and manual share CRUD as what the method exposes; the share object's own header says manual rows are what a user creates through the route and rule rows are what the evaluator materialises; ADR-0111 D4 and D7 treat every non-manual kind as evaluator-owned (not manually revocable, coexisting by kind). The two input fields stay on `GrantShareInput` because the system path uses them. A consumer loses only a call the contract never described as theirs.

Refuse over coerce is the right arm for this rule: a coerced grant would answer 201 for a request whose stated kind was not honoured, which AGENTS.md's silent-degradation test forbids; the refusal is loud, typed, carries the remedy, and costs the refused caller nothing.

`sharing-service.ts` against the contract it implements: agrees. The check sits on the non-system branch only, ahead of the posture and authorization pre-flights, and the system branch is byte-unchanged. Placement in the service rather than the route is correct, since the service is the one chokepoint every present and future non-system caller passes.

No must-fix. Two should-fix (S1, S2), three nits.

> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
